content:
Maya Rao: heads up — I sketched a proposal for v2 of the GPU telemetry/dashboard and wanted quick sync before i turn it into a PR

Jonah Li: cool, love a sketch. high level?

Maya Rao: move from single 'card health' gauge -> composable healthscore made of buckets: ECC rate, XID burst rate, thermal variance, driver resets, and inference error rate. each component has a weight + decay.

Priya Patel: sounds sensible. any thoughts on weights? ECC/XID should be high but we also don't want noisy drains for transient blips.

Maya Rao: initial idea: ECC=0.30, XID=0.28, thermal=0.15, resets=0.15, inference-errors=0.12. use short-term and long-term windows (1m, 1h, 24h) and a hysteresis policy for drains.

Sam Ortiz: can we express detection in prometheus queries? would like to see concrete panels and alert rules.

Maya Rao: yep, here's a starter PromQL for XID burst scoring:

```
sum_over_time(gpu_xid_errors_total{region="$region"}[5m])
/
max(sum_over_time(gpu_requests_total{region="$region"}[5m]), 1)
```

Then bucketize: if 5m ratio > 0.002 and 1h ratio > 0.0008 -> increment XID score.

Priya Patel: i like the two-window approach. reduces false positives. also suggest using median thermal deviation rather than mean (robust to warmup spikes).

Jonah Li: ops implications: what SLOs do we set? per-region availability of GPU capacity (not single-card) or per-card health SLO?

Maya Rao: proposal: two SLOs: 1) Regional GPU capacity SLO (99.9% of time enough usable cards to meet serving pools) 2) Fleet health SLO: weighted average healthscore across active cards >= 0.95. failure budgets tracked per-region.

Sam Ortiz: runtime/drain policy? we keep cards with score between 0.6-0.8 in a 'watch' pool and don't drain unless it dips <0.6 for 30m OR if score drops >0.2 in 10m.

Priya Patel: add manual override and canary: automated drains only in low-traffic windows + require 2 signals (XID or ECC + resets).

Maya Rao: also adding cost-control: before auto-replacing a card, check monthly replacement budget; if over budget, escalate to oncall and cheaper fallback (move traffic, pin model quantized)

ops-bot: ALERT: us-west-2 gpu_xid_rate spiked 3.2x for rack=rack-17 at 1765432160 — routed to #eng-runtime-oncall

Jonah Li: perfect timing — this is the pattern we want to catch. can we add a panel that highlights recent spikes mapped to rack and machine id?

Maya Rao: yes — new panel: 'XID hotspot heatmap' with a table: rack, machine, xid_5m_ratio, xid_1h_ratio, healthscore. clickable row opens node runbook.

Sam Ortiz: runbook checklist draft: 1) check ECC/XID logs via /infra/gpu/logs?node=ID 2) check driver/firmware versions 3) try soft-reset (ccminer -r) 4) move workloads off node 5) schedule firmware or RMA if persistent >72h

Priya Patel: add step 0: verify it's not a network congestion-induced artifact (we saw false XID spikes when PCIe resets from bad switch). command: `ethtool -S ethX | grep tx_err`

Maya Rao: nice. for dashboards, panels we need: composite healthscore, per-component sparklines, heatmap, regional SLO burn-down, and a 'cost impact if drained' estimator (how many reserved vs spot GPUs will need to be used).

Jonah Li: alert severities: P0 for region capacity drop, P1 for persistent rack-level (>3 nodes) health degrade, P2 for single-card watchlist. Use routed channels: P0 -> eng-sre + paging, P1 -> eng-runtime + ops-oncall, P2 -> just channel.

Sam Ortiz: can we auto-import new GKE node labels into Grafana so panels show tier (dedicated vs pooled) + model affinity? avoids manual lookup.

Maya Rao: yes — use the node exporter labels and an extraction job. i'll add that to the monitoring infra PR.

Priya Patel: one more: anomaly detection using rolling median absolute deviation for each metric and alert on z-score > 6. less noisy than static thresholds.

Maya Rao: agreed. action items:
- Maya: open PR with dashboard JSON + prom rules + runbook snippets (ETA EOD Tue)
- Jonah: draft SLO doc and failure budget calc by region (ETA Thu)
- Priya: refine detection windows + MAD-based anomaly logic + test against last 90d (ETA Wed)
- Sam: add runbook steps for network/firmware checks (ETA Wed)

Jonah Li: tagging @ops-oncall for awareness.

ops-bot: Note: this thread linked to alert 1765432160 (us-west-2 xid spike); auto-created incident id INC-2024-84

Maya Rao: thanks all. i'll post the PR and link back here. if anyone has strong objections to weights or drain hysteresis, call it out now or in the PR.
